biography: Martial Chouvel, a name whispered with a mix of excitement and exasperation in the Belgian racing circles, emerged from the Ardennes forests, not unlike the legendary Spa-Francorchamps circuit itself. His father, a local rally enthusiast, introduced him to the smell of burning rubber and high-octane fuel at a young age. Martial's first taste of competitive racing came at 16 in a karting championship, where his raw speed was undeniable, but his consistency was, even then, a glaring issue. He'd either win by a mile or crash out spectacularly. This inconsistency has followed him throughout his career, a double-edged sword that makes him both thrilling and frustrating to watch. After a stint in Formula Ford, he found his niche in GT racing, specifically with the Ultima GTR, a car as temperamental and demanding as Martial himself. Now at 34, he's considered to be at the peak of his career, still chasing that elusive championship title, hoping to finally harness his talent.
drivingStyle: Chouvel's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward approach. He's known for his late braking and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the car to its absolute limit. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he tends to overdrive the car early in the race, relying on raw speed to compensate. When under pressure, he can either crack and make unforced errors, or elevate his performance to an almost superhuman level. It's a gamble, but when it pays off, it's a sight to behold.

rivalries.name: Alessandro Rossi
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial overtake at the 24 Hours of Spa, resulting in both cars retiring.

rivalries.name: Ingrid Svensson
rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles, with Svensson representing calculated precision and Chouvel pure, untamed aggression.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: They've repeatedly fought for podium positions, often resulting in spectacular wheel-to-wheel battles and occasional on-track incidents.

quirks: He always wears the same lucky blue socks, no matter the weather.
He insists on listening to a specific obscure Belgian techno track before every race.
He carries a small, worn-out teddy bear, a childhood memento, in his racing bag.
famousQuote: "You either go flat out, or you go home. There's no in-between."
careerHighlight: Winning the 6 Hours of Silverstone in 2020 after a nail-biting final lap, where he overtook two cars to secure the victory. It was a masterclass in aggressive driving.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2022 due to a mechanical failure, costing his team a potential victory. He was inconsolable.
